description: Divide each film's rental_rate by its rental_duration, then average those ratios within each rating.

a.request: For each film `rating`, work out a per-day rental price: divide each film's `rental_rate` by its own `rental_duration`, then average those per-film ratios over the rating's films, ignoring missing values. Then average these per-rating figures across ratings, again ignoring missing values, and keep the ratings strictly above that average (none if it is missing). Return one row: the average per-day figure of those ratings and the average amount by which they exceed the across-rating average, both ignoring missing values and unrounded.
a.sql: WITH rating_averages AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / NULLIF(rental_duration, 0)) AS avg_per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(avg_per_day) AS avg_per_day FROM rating_averages) SELECT AVG(r.avg_per_day) AS avg_per_day_above_average, AVG(r.avg_per_day - o.avg_per_day) AS avg_excess FROM rating_averages AS r CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o WHERE r.avg_per_day > o.avg_per_day

c.request: For each film `rating`, what is the average rental price per day (`rental_rate` per day of `rental_duration`), ignoring missing values? Average those per-rating figures across ratings and keep the ratings strictly above that average (none if it is missing). Give me one row: the average per-day price of those ratings and how far above the across-rating average they are on average, ignoring missing values and unrounded. Divide each film's rental_rate by its rental_duration, then average those ratios within each rating.
c.sql: WITH rating_averages AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / NULLIF(rental_duration, 0)) AS avg_per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(avg_per_day) AS avg_across_ratings FROM rating_averages) SELECT AVG(r.avg_per_day) AS avg_per_day_above_average, AVG(r.avg_per_day - o.avg_across_ratings) AS avg_amount_above_average FROM rating_averages r CROSS JOIN overall_average o WHERE r.avg_per_day > o.avg_across_ratings

b.request: For each rating, average each film’s unrounded `rental_rate / rental_duration`, ignoring missing ratios; average those rating averages, retain ratings strictly above that overall average (none if it is missing), and return one row with the retained ratings’ average per-day price and their average amount above the overall average, ignoring missing values
b.sql: WITH rating_averages AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / NULLIF(rental_duration, 0)) AS avg_per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(avg_per_day) AS avg_per_day FROM rating_averages) SELECT AVG(r.avg_per_day) AS retained_avg_per_day, AVG(r.avg_per_day - o.avg_per_day) AS avg_amount_above_overall FROM rating_averages AS r CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o WHERE r.avg_per_day > o.avg_per_day

d.request: For each film, divide `rental_rate` by `rental_duration`, then average those ratios within each `rating`, ignoring missing values. Average the per-rating results across ratings and keep only ratings strictly above that average (none if the average is missing). Return one row with the unrounded average per-day price of the retained ratings and their unrounded average difference from the across-rating average, ignoring missing values.
d.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), across_ratings AS (SELECT AVG(avg_per_day) AS overall_avg_per_day FROM per_rating) SELECT AVG(pr.avg_per_day) AS avg_per_day_price, AVG(pr.avg_per_day - ar.overall_avg_per_day) AS avg_difference FROM per_rating AS pr CROSS JOIN across_ratings AS ar WHERE pr.avg_per_day > ar.overall_avg_per_day
